title: Turned a pasted list into a MindNode map in one command

brief.why: MindNode refuses to paste a multi-line list as separate nodes, and its library is a CloudKit-synced CRDT operation log that must not be hand-edited. OPML import is the only safe route in, and its two silent failure modes make a hand-rolled attempt look like it worked.
brief.what: The arete CLI plus the mindnode-mapping skill, installed and shipping from spm1001/arete.
brief.done: arete reads the clipboard, lands a verified map in MindNode, and exits non-zero when it does not.

title: Arete reaches maps it cannot currently touch, via MindNode's App Intents

brief.why: Two real gaps, and one supported route closes both. OPML import always creates a NEW document, so nodes cannot be added to an existing map. And --extract reads only base snapshots, so it refuses on any map typed in the app (content lives in an unfolded CRDT operation log). MindNode's own App Intents solve both: ExportDocumentIntent exports Markdown from the LIVE document, and CreateNodeIntent places a node childOf/siblingAfter an existing one.
brief.what: A Shortcut per direction, plus arete learning to call 'shortcuts run' — so --extract works on every map and there is a way to append to an open map.
brief.done: arete can extract 'My Areas of Focus' (285 unfolded operations, currently refused) and can add a node to an existing map.
brief.how: No supported way to invoke an app intent from a shell, so one Shortcut must be built by hand in Shortcuts.app; 'shortcuts run <name>' is scriptable after that. Intent list: python3 -c "import json,pathlib;d=json.loads(pathlib.Path('/Applications/MindNode.app/Contents/Resources/Metadata.appintents/extract.actionsdata').read_text());print(sorted(d['actions']))". Check whether shortcuts run can take a document parameter, or whether one Shortcut per map is needed.

title: Arete extracts maps typed in the app, not just imported ones

brief.why: A snapshot is a base. Maps typed in MindNode keep their content in a CRDT operation log against an all-but-empty 324-byte snapshot, so --extract currently refuses on them — 2 of the 4 maps in the library. Replaying the log is the deep fix; the App Intents item is the shallow one and may make this unnecessary.
brief.what: Either an operation-log replay in arete, or a decision that the App Intents route makes it redundant.
brief.done: Either 'arete --extract' works on a map with unfolded operations and matches MindNode's own Markdown export byte-for-byte, or this is closed as superseded.
brief.how: Operations look like character-range text edits with hybrid logical clocks — a real CRDT replay whose failure mode is SILENT wrongness. Do not ship it without diffing against MindNode's own export on several maps as the oracle. Consider doing the App Intents item first and closing this one.

title: Arete is installable the way the rest of the suite is

brief.why: It is built to the suite's conventions (skills/<name>/SKILL.md, hatchling, bon) but nothing has been added to the batterie-de-savoir marketplace, so it installs only from a local path. Meanwhile the skill is DEPLOYED as a copy at ~/.claude/skills/mindnode-mapping/SKILL.md so it actually loads — the repo is upstream, that copy is a deployment, exactly like a rules/ shard. Two copies is the drift risk this item closes.
brief.what: Either a plugin entry in batterie-de-savoir (and then DELETE ~/.claude/skills/mindnode-mapping/ so there is no plugin/user duplicate), or a note saying local-install-only is deliberate and the deployed copy is the permanent home.
brief.done: Either 'claude plugin install arete@batterie' works and the user-skill copy is gone, or the decision is written down in the repo CLAUDE.md.

title: Re-check whether MindNode's MCP server can be enabled

brief.why: MindNode 2026.4.4 ships a complete automation MCP server (add_nodes, move_nodes, create_connection) that would allow adding nodes to an EXISTING map — the one thing OPML import cannot do. On 2026-08-28 it could not be switched on: the autostart pref is reset by the app on launch, nothing listens, no token is minted. Undetermined whether that is a Plus gate or unreleased.
brief.what: A verdict: Plus-gated, unreleased, or live — and if live, arete gaining an add-to-existing-map path.
brief.done: Either a listener answers on MindNode's MCP port, or we have written down which of the two gates it is.
brief.how: defaults read com.ideasoncanvas.mindnode MNDefaultsMCPServerShouldAutoStartOnLaunch; lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN -a -p $(pgrep -x MindNode). Cheapest real test is taking the backToSchool Plus promo and looking in Settings.
